transcription.name: Pinyin
transcription.note: Hanyu Pinyin. The wikitext attempt reads the |m= parameter of every {{zh-pron}} template on the page, which Wiktionary keeps as the canonical Mandarin reading; a comma separates alternative readings and each is shown. 'normalize' is on so the alternatives are split, and Pinyin carries no delimiter it could strip. The same parameter also carries markers after a comma, such as 1nb= for a note on the first reading or er=y for an erhua form, so the pattern stops at the first piece holding an equals sign. The HTML attempt is the fallback, reading the Latn span of every Hanyu Pinyin line of the rendered pronunciation box with the span strategy, because the line nests a link and a phonetic note the flat pattern would take too; each alternative is printed as its own line. The article page is asked before the REST rendering, because the REST host rejects bursts with 429. A simplified-form or variant-form page carries no reading of its own and only points at its main form through {{zh-see}}, so the wikitext attempt follows that pointer and the later attempts ask for the form it named.

transcription.name: Bopomofo
transcription.note: Zhuyin. Wiktionary derives it from the Pinyin at render time, so only the rendered page carries it, as the Bopo span of the Zhuyin line. Every Zhuyin line of the box is read, one per alternative reading. The box also opens with a summary line joining every alternative with a comma, and that line closes its label with a bracket before the small tag, so the match anchors on the label without the bracket and keeps the summary out. The article page is asked before the REST rendering, because the REST host rejects bursts with 429. A simplified-form page only points at its main form, so the attempt follows the see link of the rendered page.

glyph.name: Traditional
glyph.note: The traditional form the entry is written in, one transcription row under the scheme named here, and the language each character opens an entry in. The wikitext attempt reads the {{zh-see}} pointer a simplified-form or variant-form page carries, which names the traditional main form; a page that is already traditional carries none, the lookup finds nothing, and the reading view shows the headword's own characters. The pointer's later parameters are cut at the first bar, so a page with a second pointer yields a second candidate.

note: Language pack for Mandarin. Every URL and extraction rule is data — edit here, no recompile. The 'pronunciation' and 'audio' lists are independent and each is shown in the order written here. The pronunciation sources publish IPA, while Pinyin and Zhuyin are the transcription schemes above. No morphology sources are listed, because Mandarin words do not inflect. Every source is read from an ordinary article page rather than a machine API, because the article hosts impose no request ceiling while the REST endpoints reject bursts with 429, which the reader would report as an unreachable source. A simplified-form page only points at its traditional form, so every attempt follows the see link of the rendered page.

pronunciation.name: Wiktionary
pronunciation.note: The Chinese pronunciation table of an entry carries one row per variety. Only the Mandarin row links its IPA key to the Mandarin pronunciation appendix, so that link anchors the reader to the right row and keeps Cantonese, Hakka and Min readings out. Every such row on the page is read, one per alternative reading and per etymology. The see link is followed even when the page has readings of its own, because a character can be both a word and the simplified form of another. The span strategy is required because the transcription nests tone-note spans inside the IPA span, which a flat pattern would truncate. An entry with no Mandarin section carries no anchor, so the attempt simply yields nothing.

pronunciation.name: Chinese Wiktionary
pronunciation.note: The Chinese Wiktionary prints the same transcription behind a Chinese anchor, where the key of the Mandarin row links to the Wiktionary:漢語發音表記 page and the label reads 幫助. The regional Mandarin rows and every other variety link their key to an encyclopedia article instead, so the anchor keeps them out. Its coverage of Mandarin headwords is thinner than the English one, so it stands second. A simplified-form page carries no reading of its own and only points at its traditional form through a 請見 box, so the attempt follows that pointer.

audio.name: Naver
audio.note: Naver Chinese-Korean dictionary search API, the same shape as the English pack's Naver source. Each entry carries a 'symbolFile' holding a female recording and a male recording, joined with a bar, each an opaque token-bearing mp3 address that the file host rejects without its token. The first entry matched exactly is taken, whether as an entry or as a sub-entry, because a traditional headword lands on the simplified entry as a sub-entry, and the anchor at the start of the body keeps every later entry out; an idiom entry ahead of it carries a bare identifier rather than an address and is passed over. Two untagged readings take the female and the male address from that one match. The API returns an empty body without a Referer header, so one is declared here.

audio.name: Daum
audio.note: Daum Chinese-Korean dictionary. The search page answers in one of two shapes. A headword with one exact entry gets no list, only a meta refresh pointing at the entry page by its wordid, so the first attempt captures that wordid as its follow value and the second attempt asks the entry page for it, where the recording address stands in the wordPronFileUrl script variable; the hop the follow spends re-searching the wordid itself finds nothing and costs one fetch. A headword with several entries, or none, gets a list, where each entry prints its headword in a txt_cleansch or txt_searchword link, the matched part wrapped in an emphasis span, and its recording as a data-url on the listen button; the pattern takes every entry whose whole headword is exactly {word}, so a list of related words for an unknown headword yields nothing. The addresses are printed with a plain http scheme, so only the host and path are captured and 'prefix' supplies https. The entry page refuses a bare Mozilla/5.0 user agent, but accepts the engine's own. A traditional headword finds no entry, because the dictionary is keyed on simplified forms.

audio.name: Wiktionary
audio.note: Wiktionary embeds Commons recordings as protocol-relative addresses, so 'prefix' supplies the scheme. Only the transcoded mp3 rendition is taken, because the original is OGG or WAV. A Mandarin recording is either a Lingua Libre LL-Q9192_%28cmn%29- file or a Zh- file, and the Zh- files of a page are also written Zh_ with an underscore, so both separators are taken. The Zh- prefix must not continue as Zh-yue- or Zh-nan-, which mark the Cantonese and Min Nan recordings of the same page. One attempt reads both, so the page is fetched once. A simplified-form page only points at its traditional form, so the attempt follows the see link.

audio.name: Wikimedia Commons
audio.note: Most Mandarin recordings on Commons are never embedded on a Wiktionary page, so the file store is searched directly. The search asks for files whose title carries the headword and the cmn tag, which every Lingua Libre LL-Q9192 (cmn)- file carries, and the API answers with the transcoded renditions of each file found. Search matches by character, so a title holding the headword inside a longer phrase is returned too; the pattern therefore takes only a file whose title ends in exactly {word}. Only the mp3 rendition is taken, because the original is WAV. utf8=1 keeps the title readable so the headword can be matched, and formatversion=2 keeps the addresses unescaped.

frequency.name: Purple Culture
frequency.note: Purple Culture's dictionary page marks a word on the HSK vocabulary lists with a green badge holding HSK 1 to HSK 6, the headword badge first when compounds below carry their own. The page title names the word looked up, so the confirm guard fails for a spelling the dictionary does not know, and a word outside the HSK lists has no badge, so either way the attempt yields nothing. A traditional spelling resolves to the same page as its simplified form.
